annotationRationale: The problem connects coordinate area with logarithmic identities. Logarithm monotonicity justifies the vertex configuration and equality of arguments, while factoring resolves the resulting quadratic. Trapezoid subtraction and shoelace remain separate route-specific concepts.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Algebra is a reasonable classification for the logarithmic equation arising from coordinate area. No obvious subject repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Writing the coordinates as n,n+1,n+2,n+3 gives area ln((n+1)(n+2)/(n(n+3))). Equating arguments yields n(n+3)=180, whose only positive root is 12. The stem, choices and key D agree; there is no figure contradiction.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank methods are supplied. Both useful reference routes are retained: AoPS Solution 3's trapezoid subtraction and LIVE/AoPS shoelace. The reference choice-testing and factor observations merely finish the same equation and need no additional method.
review.annotationCheck: Coordinate area and logarithmic operations are appropriate assessed concepts. Logarithm monotonicity and quadratic factoring are support concepts; trapezoid subtraction and shoelace are accurately distinguished at method level.
review.areaCheck: Algebra is a reasonable classification for the logarithmic equation arising from coordinate area. No obvious subject repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The consecutive secant slopes strictly decrease, placing the two middle vertices above the closing chord. The three width-one trapezoids minus the width-three trapezoid give y1+y2−y0−y3. Logarithm laws then give the stated ratio and roots 12 and −15; positivity selects 12.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The claimed AoPS Solution 3 basis is accurate. The secant-slope justification and self-contained notation supply an independently explained version of the reference argument. source-informed-original correctly identifies the nonofficial source.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why trapezoids fit. Vertex placement, both area expressions, logarithm injectivity and the quadratic transition are sufficiently justified without calculus or an external diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Coordinate area, trapezoid area, composite-area subtraction, logarithm operations, logarithm monotonicity and factoring all appear explicitly. No unexplained concavity technique is hidden behind a broad node.

F-BF.B.5 and F-IF.C.7e overlap only through logarithm work, not full inverse-function or graphing coverage. Factoring fits the relevant A-REI.B.4/4b and A-SSE.B.3a components.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The direct concepts precisely describe the derivation. The decreasing-slope configuration is derived from mapped logarithm operations and monotonicity.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Translation preserves area, and decreasing slopes justify boundary order. The displayed shoelace products simplify to |y1+y2−y0−y3|. The logarithm is positive because its numerator exceeds its denominator by 2. The resulting equation has the unique positive solution n=12.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: LIVE and AoPS Solutions 1 and 2 support the claimed shoelace route. The translated coordinates simplify the calculation independently, and the algebraic finish matches LIVE. Nonofficial influence is correctly labeled source-informed-original.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The translation has a clear purpose, and the explanation states the shoelace rule before applying it. Boundary order, absolute-value removal and root selection are explained.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: The exact shoelace node is used rather than substituting generic coordinate geometry. Logarithm operations, monotonicity and factoring all match the written steps.
